chapter: New York, Philadelphia and Harlem nightlife
title: Tallulah Bankhead bars Billy Rose and the show closes
summary: Bankhead bars Rose from the theater after a dispute and the show closes.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Now, we rehearsed this show; we tried out in Detroit; we played Philadelphia; and one day in New York when we were getting ready to open, Tallulah Bankhead went up on the right side of the theater and there was a scene where that you could not see her, you know, for that's like a fleeting moment. She would disappear from view. And she said to Billy, and God for me to give me if they don't want tell what happened. She said to Billy, "Billy, I'm lost." And then she recited lines, "And you will go in a daddledede-dat." Then she's back in view. Do you know that she told him to change that and he wouldn't. And she barred him from the theater. She wouldn't let him come in the theater. She said, "If you come in here, I'm not doing the show." And he had to stay away, so the show finally closed. It later became a very successful movie, but they didn't carry out the idea about the music, I don't think. I don't...
As far as I remember, no.
Because that whole thing was just "Freight Train Blues," you know, that kind of, you know what I mean, you know,

triplets, you know, thirds, and, you know what I mean, things like that, and tremolo. But the show closed, and it later became a movie, but I don't think that that movie carried the theme which would have been, you know...maybe they perhaps could have used a clarinet to play, you know what I mean crescendoes and all that business.
